title: T11: connector catalog and click-only Gmail/Outlook connect flows
head: codex/t11-connect-flows
body:
T11 adds the connector catalog and click-only OAuth 2.0 connect flows. `catalog/` holds one `connector.yaml` per connector (Gmail, Outlook, Outlook Calendar, Google Calendar, OneDrive, Google Drive, Teams) with plain-words `setup_steps` and error messages. `src/gates/connect.py` opens the provider's consent page in the browser, receives the callback on `127.0.0.1`, exchanges the code via PKCE, stores the token through the secrets interface, tests the connection with one read call, and silently refreshes on expiry or 401. No terminal, no API keys, no manual token handling — the person sees only what they need to click and plain-words confirmations or errors. Every connector requests the least-privilege read scope Phase 0 needs; Google Cloud and Microsoft Entra registrations (T03) are configured once per provider and reused across all connectors for that provider.

Entry points: `python -m gates.status` shows every connector's status (Connected / Not connected / Needs attention), and `python -m gates.connect connect <name>` runs one flow. Tokens store a full bundle (access, refresh, expiry, scopes) through `anorak.secrets`, refreshing proactively within 60 seconds of expiry and reactively once on 401; status checks expiry locally without touching the network. Security: loopback listener on a random free port, state checked before any network call, PKCE on every flow, no redirects followed, HTTP timeouts and response-size bounds, tokens and error details never in logs or error output. Tests cover the full flow against fake Google-shaped and fake Microsoft-shaped servers, forced expiry with silent refresh, 401-triggered retry, denied flows, state and PKCE mismatches, and every error path — 197 passed.

Validation:
```
.venv/bin/pytest -q
197 passed in 2.04s
.venv/bin/ruff check .
All checks passed!
.venv/bin/mypy --strict src/
Success: no issues found in 12 source files
```

Every test runs against loopback OAuth servers with fake client IDs and tokens — no live provider call was made. Braden's live click-through of Gmail and Outlook, including token storage to the keychain and status confirmation, is pending as the human acceptance step; tests cover the full flow and every error path, but clicking a real "Allow" button and proving a real token survives are acceptance steps, not automated ones. Google Cloud OAuth is in Testing mode with Braden as the only approved tester; Gmail, Google Calendar and Google Drive carry setup-step copy explaining the "Google hasn't verified this app" interstitial and error copy explaining that a Testing-mode refresh token expires after 7 days (tracked locally as `refresh_ttl_days=7`, an assumption not verified against Google's live behaviour). Microsoft admin consent for the OASIS app is granted (`docs/registrations.md`), so Outlook, Outlook Calendar, OneDrive and Teams are releasable as far as this ticket is concerned. Two follow-ups for coordinated completion: (1) `connector.yaml` uses fields beyond the T10 `formats.md` sample (`display_name`, `description`, `sensitivity`, `oauth.*`, `connection_test.*`, `notes`); recommend folding these into `formats.md` with a `docs/DECISIONS.md` entry rather than leaving them a T11-only extension. (2) Outlook Calendar and Google Calendar have only read+write scopes registered (`Calendars.ReadWrite`, `calendar.events`); if a true read-only variant should be added to the Microsoft and Google app registrations, that is a T03/T03b follow-up, not a T11 code change. Package version 0.2.0 with agent-core 0.4.0 pinned via vendored wheel; no release published. Base branch main (T03).
